questions: Did the movements begin suddenly, reaching their worst within minutes or hours?
Did they begin within the last few days?
Have you developed weakness or clumsiness on either side of your body?
Have you had numbness or loss of sensation on either side?
Has one side of your face drooped?
Have you had difficulty speaking, understanding speech, swallowing, walking, or seeing?
Have you experienced a sudden severe headache, dizziness, or loss of balance?
Have you had any loss of awareness, staring spells, or confusion?
Do the movements stop completely when you are asleep?
Do the movements lessen when you deliberately hold the affected limb still?
Have you ever had similar movements before?
Do you have diabetes?
Have you recently had very high blood-sugar readings, excessive thirst, or frequent urination?
Have you recently started, stopped, or changed the dose of any medication?
Do you take antipsychotic, nausea, Parkinson’s, seizure, stimulant, or antidepressant medication?
Have you used cocaine, amphetamines, or other recreational drugs recently?
Have you recently had a fever, significant infection, head injury, or exposure to toxins?
Are you pregnant or within one year after giving birth?
Have you or a close relative had a similar movement disorder?
Have you had liver disease, unexplained jaundice, or psychiatric or movement symptoms beginning in adolescence or early adulthood?

dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Nonketotic hyperglycemia–induced hemichorea (diabetic striatopathy), caused by severe uncontrolled diabetes mellitus

ALTERNATIVE: Small basal-ganglia ischemic stroke

ALTERNATIVE: Nonketotic hyperglycemia–associated basal-ganglia hemorrhagic change

ALTERNATIVE: Drug-induced chorea or hemiballismus

3. Plasma glucose, serum osmolality, and HbA1c

5. Complete blood count, liver function tests, and thyroid-stimulating hormone

dx: Nonketotic hyperglycemia–induced hemichorea (diabetic striatopathy), caused by severe uncontrolled diabetes mellitus
